answer: "cited_page_ids=['paper.graphrag-2024', 'paper.lightrag-2025', 'paper.leanrag-2025', 'paper.cuprate-expert-eval-2025', 'ent.llm-judged-win-rate'] answer_markdown='## 1) Direct answer\\nLLM-judged win rates provide, at best, a **partial and task-/metric-dependent proxy** for factual quality in RAG comparisons: there is some evidence they correlate with *count-based* proxies for \u201ccomprehensiveness/diversity\u201d in one setting, but multiple sources caution that these evaluations are **not grounded in factual-accuracy metrics**, can be **structurally biased toward certain answer styles**, and can **change system orderings** when you switch evaluation metrics or protocols.\\n\\n## 2) Evidence for side A (they track factual quality reasonably / have some validity)\\n- GraphRAG reports a measurable (though imperfect) agreement between LLM-judge labels and a claim-count proxy: \\n  - Quote: \u201cthe aggregated LLM label matched the claim-based label in **78%** of pairwise comparisons for comprehensiveness and **69-70%** for diversity\u201d (paper.graphrag-2024#findings, ^c10).\\n\\n## 3) Evidence for side B (they do *not* reliably track factual quality / are weakly validated)\\n- LightRAG\u2019s evaluation is explicitly judge-preference without factual grounding:\\n  - Quote: \u201cEvidence caveat: all results are **LLM-judged win rates** on LLM-generated questions; **no factual-accuracy metric**.\u201d (paper.lightrag-2025#tl_dr).\\n  - Quote: \u201cWe employ a robust LLM, specifically **GPT-4o-mini, to rank** each baseline against our LightRAG\u201d and \u201cno factual-accuracy or groundedness metric is reported.\u201d (paper.lightrag-2025#findings, ^c10).\\n- GraphRAG\u2019s own limitations emphasize that its evaluation does not establish factual correctness and is narrow in task coverage:\\n  - Quote: \u201cevaluation covers **only global sensemaking questions**\u2026; **no fabrication-rate comparison**\u2026 Local/factoid QA is never evaluated\u201d (paper.graphrag-2024#limitations).\\n  - Quote: \u201cwinning criteria (comprehensiveness, diversity) structurally favor **long, many-claim answers**\u2026 but doesn\u2019t measure **correctness**\u201d (paper.graphrag-2024#limitations).\\n- LeanRAG likewise uses LLMs as judges and provides no factual-accuracy calibration:\\n  - Quote: \u201cwe use **DeepSeek-V3 \u2026 as our evaluators**\u2026 and each query and answer is scored 5 times\u201d and \u201cno ground-truth **factual-accuracy**\u2026 metric is reported.\u201d (paper.leanrag-2025#findings, ^c13).\\n- The \u201cLLM-judged win rate\u201d entry explicitly warns that metric/protocol choice can flip conclusions:\\n  - Quote: \u201cswitching from win-rate to extractive token-F1 **inverts system orderings**\u2026 Metric choice is outcome-determining.\u201d (ent.llm-judged-win-rate#evidence).\\n  - Quote: \u201cPairwise protocol separates systems that pointwise 1-10 scoring calls equal\u2026 protocol choice changes apparent margins on identical answers.\u201d (ent.llm-judged-win-rate#evidence).\\n- Expert evaluation is positioned as a contrasting \u201cground truth\u201d precisely because LLM-judged RAG evals don\u2019t provide that level of factual vetting:\\n  - Quote: \u201cTrustworthy answers\u2026 must be grounded in vetted experiments\u2026 The study is positioned as uniquely expensive **ground truth**: only world experts can grade answers at this level, unlike **LLM-judged RAG evals**\u201d (paper.cuprate-expert-eval-2025#context).\\n\\n## 4) Conditions / when each side applies (if supported)\\n- **More defensible as a proxy** when your target dimensions resemble *comprehensiveness/diversity* and you can tolerate proxy validation rather than truth: GraphRAG\u2019s agreement with claim-count labels is reported specifically for those dimensions (paper.graphrag-2024#findings, ^c10).\\n- **Less defensible for factual quality** when (a) the study reports \u201cno factual-accuracy metric\u201d (paper.lightrag-2025#tl_dr; paper.lightrag-2025#findings, ^c10; paper.leanrag-2025#findings, ^c13), (b) tasks are limited to \u201cglobal sensemaking\u201d rather than \u201clocal/factoid QA\u201d (paper.graphrag-2024#limitations), or (c) different evaluation metrics/protocols might change ordering (\u201cinverts system orderings\u201d; \u201cprotocol choice changes apparent margins\u201d) (ent.llm-judged-win-rate#evidence).\\n\\n## 5) Page ids relied on (paper.* / ent.* only)\\n- paper.graphrag-2024\\n- paper.lightrag-2025\\n- paper.leanrag-2025\\n- ent.llm-judged-win-rate\\n- paper.cuprate-expert-eval-2025'"
